entities.summary:
Cosma Orsini was an Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a significant role in the High Renaissance.

Born into a noble family in Rome, Cosma was ordained as a priest at 28 and rose to become Archbishop of Siena in 1450. He later became cardinal-deacon of Sant'Angelo in Pesaro under Pope Nicholas V.

Orsini's influence extended beyond his ecclesiastical duties, as he was also a patron of the arts and architecture. His contributions to the construction of St. Peter's Basilica are particularly notable.

Cosma Orsini died on November 30, 1481, at the age of 91, leaving behind a legacy that continues to shape the Catholic Church and Italian Renaissance art.

One striking statistic is that Cosma was one of the most influential cardinals of his time, participating in over 200 papal conclaves between 1450 and 1485.

The cardinal's commitment to education and the arts led to the establishment of several institutions, including the College of Cardinalis at Rome.

Cosma Orsini was also known for his diplomatic efforts, serving as a key mediator in relations between the Holy Roman Empire and the Papal States.

In conclusion, Cosma Orsini's enduring impact on Catholic Church history and Renaissance art makes him an important figure to study in the context of 15th-century Italy.
